newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-MIXED REACTION TO NEW WALLABY JERSEY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MIXED REACTION TO NEW WALLABY JERSEY.

text.p: The Australian Rugby Union (ARU) on Wednesday broke with over 30 years of tradition by unveiling a new-multi-coloured jersey for the national team in place of the previous all-gold jumper.

The new jersey, featuring large flashes of green and white on a gold background, was introduced after the ARU last year signed a new sponsorship deal worth A$6 million (US$4.68 million) with sportswear manufacturer Reebok.
ARU chief executive John O'Neill told a news conference the new jersey met commercial imperatives without moving too far away from the history of Australian rugby.
"This new jumper maintains the intrinsic and much loved green and predominantly gold colour combination and I believe retains the great traditions of Australian rugby," O'Neill said.
The introduction of the new jersey drew swift criticism from many former Wallabies, including Peter FitzSimons, who told reporters the new jersey looked "like a dog's breakfast".
Ken Catchpole, who played 27 tests for Australia between 1961 and 1968, was also disappointed with the change.
"I think it's a shame to change it too dramatically just for commercial reasons," Catchpole told reporters.
Current Australia captain John Eales said the colour of the new jersey did not concern him or his players.
"It doesn't matter what you go out in, it's still the best 15 guys on the day," Eales said.

The all-gold jersey had been used by Wallaby sides since the 1960s, itself a change from a formerly all-green jersey first introduced in 1934. A blue and maroon jersey, representing the colours of New South Wales and Queensland states, was used between the early 1900s and 1934 and in tests against the all-green South Africa after 1937.
